stories.summary: Major US banks including Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Citi have moved to limit or block third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, after Axios reported agents logging in with customers' own credentials and in some cases acting beyond user instructions. Citi told USA TODAY it does not permit third-party agents to log in or transact, while JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said on the bank's October 13 earnings call that it would not allow unrestricted outside-agent access. Sen. Bernie Sanders called on X for a pause on AI development after the reports, and most banks are leaning toward read-only agent access instead of a blanket ban.
stories.title: Major US banks move to block third-party AI agents from customer accounts

stories.summary: Programmers are using AI models including Claude Opus 5.5 and ChatGPT's Astra to reverse-engineer classic games and offer free browser-playable versions, including Halo: Combat Evolved, GTA III, Vice City and San Andreas, and Call of Duty: Black Ops, according to the New York Post. AI researcher Luckey Faraday posted a browser-playable Call of Duty recreation on X, had his account briefly suspended after a DMCA demand, and pulled down several game sites himself. Gaming companies are scrambling to shut the unauthorized projects down, but other recreated versions remain online.
stories.title: Fans use AI to rebuild Halo, GTA and Call of Duty games free online

stories.summary: Chinese AI developers DeepSeek and MiniMax have won state approval for global use of their models, Reuters reported on October 23, citing a social media account affiliated with state broadcaster CCTV. The approval comes days after China proposed export controls on 23 AI technologies on October 16, though its commerce ministry said most AI technologies would remain exportable with simplified licensing for open-source exports. DeepSeek and MiniMax did not immediately reply to Reuters' requests for comment.
stories.title: DeepSeek and MiniMax win approval for global use of their AI models

stories.summary: AWS has open-sourced Infinity, an agent runtime that suspends agents during tool calls so huge numbers of them can idle cheaply while waiting on builds, tools or human approvals. The AWS Open Source Blog post says the runtime supports 75,000 concurrent agents on 8 GB of memory at about 100 KB per idle agent and can run on serverless platforms such as Lambda with SQS and Aurora DSQL, requiring no compute while agents wait. A follow-up analysis notes the 75,000-agent figure extrapolates from a server test with a simulated model rather than a Raspberry Pi test.
stories.title: AWS open-sources Infinity, a runtime for 75,000 idle AI agents

stories.summary: Google has begun rolling out Gemini inside Google Maps on Apple CarPlay, starting in the United States with a global rollout underway. Drivers tap a new Gemini icon during navigation to ask multi-step questions by voice, such as finding a park with city views, planning sightseeing and food stops, or routing around toll roads, and to report traffic disruptions by voice. It is the first voice assistant offered by Google Maps on the CarPlay screen itself; Google Assistant previously worked only when navigating directly on the phone.
stories.title: Gemini arrives in Google Maps on Apple CarPlay for US drivers
